name: CHI
fullName: ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
notes: Main papers track. No separate abstract deadline. Submission includes videos and supplementary materials. The official 24-hour contingency grace period is not included in the deadline shown. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Make a significant contribution to understanding or improving human interaction with technology. Systems, studies, design, theory, and other contribution types can fit when the HCI knowledge gained is clear.
guide.evidence: Use a method that supports the contribution and describe it transparently. For studies, explain sampling and analysis; for systems, establish the interaction benefit; for design or conceptual work, substantiate the argument. A user study is not a universal requirement for every contribution type.

comparisons.difference: A more focused XR audience when immersive interaction, 3D interfaces, or VR/AR systems are central.
More specialized when the key finding concerns human perception and its application to computing.

name: IEEE VR
fullName: IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces
notes: One unified submission and review process for IEEE TVCG and conference-only papers. A paper abstract is required seven days before the paper. Notification times are not specified.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

guide.contribution: Advance VR, AR, MR, or 3D interaction through a method, technique, application, or system. Explain the contribution to immersive technology or experience, beyond placing an existing task in a headset.
guide.evidence: The call asks for evaluation suited to the contribution: user studies, benchmarks, or comparisons with existing methods or systems. Measure the claimed benefit and describe experimental conditions, limitations, and participant procedures where applicable.

comparisons.difference: Strong scope overlap across AR, MR, and VR; ISMAR also explicitly requires a significant connection to XR concepts, systems, or experiences.
A broader interaction audience; emphasize the transferable HCI insight when the contribution extends beyond immersive technology.

name: ISMAR
fullName: IEEE International Symposium on Mixed and Augmented Reality
notes: Unified IEEE TVCG journal and conference paper track. The 2027 site confirms Kobe, Japan, but the conference dates and paper deadlines are still TBA; estimates use the verified 2026 schedule.

journals: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (TVCG)
publication.note: Unified review assigns accepted papers to the journal or conference proceedings.

guide.contribution: Make an explicit, significant connection to AR, MR, or VR. Contributions may concern underlying technologies, interaction, perception, systems, or applied experiences; the scope includes fully virtual environments.
guide.evidence: A useful framing is to show how the work improves an XR capability or experience. Use technical measurements for system claims and suitable studies for human-experience claims, making the XR-specific insight and limitations clear.

comparisons.difference: Both cover AR, MR, and VR. Their scopes overlap strongly, so compare the current call and the best audience for the contribution.
A closely related venue for XR software, systems, interaction techniques, and their evaluation.

name: VRST
fullName: ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology
notes: Main papers track. The abstract is required one week before the full paper. Includes the officially extended revision and final-notification dates. No official 2027 schedule was found. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Present an XR software, system, interaction, or related research contribution. Make clear what the technique or system adds and how that advances the use or understanding of immersive environments.
guide.evidence: For technical claims, useful evidence includes performance tests and comparisons; for interaction claims, consider user experience or empirical studies. Explain the contribution rather than relying on a prototype description. The call asks that paper length match the contribution.

comparisons.difference: Substantial overlap in XR systems and interaction; examine the specific paper categories and evaluation expectations.
A more targeted fit when the key advance is the integration of AI with XR, rather than an XR technique on its own.

name: ACM SAP
notes: Abstract submission is required. The paper deadline was extended from April 28. This schedule covers SAP proceedings papers; invited TAP journal papers have a separate second review and final deadline. Notification release has no exact time.

publication.note: Selected papers undergo a second review cycle and publish in TAP instead of the proceedings.

guide.contribution: Connect a question about perception with a computing problem, such as animation, visualization, vision, or immersive interfaces. Make the perceptual insight and its computational relevance explicit.
guide.evidence: For empirical work, justify the stimuli, tasks, measures, and analysis so the perceptual conclusion is supported. Explain how the result informs a computing technique or application. Perceptually informed algorithms can also fit; the contribution need not be only a user study.

comparisons.difference: Broader interaction and human-centered research; SAP is more focused on perception as the scientific link to computing.
More focused on socially interactive agents when agent behavior or human-agent interaction is the main question.

name: IEEE AIxVR
fullName: IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality
notes: Formerly IEEE AIVR; renamed AIxVR in 2024. This schedule covers full/short papers, extended from September 17 to September 21, 2026. Notifications are only specified as early-to-mid-November 2026, so no exact notification date is shown. Separate 2027 work-in-progress and demo/video tracks close October 29, 2026; workshops set their own deadlines. The source states AoE but gives no exact clock time.

core.note: No matching entry found by acronym and full title; this is not an Unranked classification.

publication.note: Selected papers are invited to submit extended versions; the 2027 call does not name the journal.

paperFit.scope: AI for XR · XR for AI

guide.contribution: Make the relationship between AI and XR central: AI that enables an immersive capability, or XR that advances the use or understanding of AI. State what the integration contributes.
guide.evidence: A useful evaluation isolates the benefit of that integration, using technical or user measures suited to the claim. Compare against a relevant alternative and explain limitations. Merely including an off-the-shelf AI component needs a clear research argument.

comparisons.difference: A broader home for XR software and interaction work whose contribution does not depend on AI.
More specialized for socially interactive agents and human-agent behavior, including applications outside XR.

name: ACM IVA
fullName: ACM International Conference on Intelligent Virtual Agents
notes: Full papers track with a separate abstract deadline. Submission dates include the published extensions; these extensions may not recur. The IVA series announces Reykjavik in September 2027, but exact event dates and paper deadlines are not published; estimates use the 2026 schedule. Notification times are not specified.

publication.note: No journal track announced in the linked call. Conference proceedings are distinct from a journal.

guide.contribution: Advance socially interactive agents or human-agent interaction: behavior generation, dialogue, social perception, agent design, or an underlying theory. Explain how the work changes agent capability or understanding of interaction.
guide.evidence: Ground the claims in appropriate technical evaluation, human studies, theory, or application evidence. For social-behavior claims, explain the behavioral model and measures; realistic appearance alone does not establish an interaction contribution.

comparisons.difference: Centers human-robot interaction, including physical embodiment and its consequences; HRI also accepts studies without a physical robot when the HRI contribution is clear.
A better-focused audience when the primary result is a perceptual mechanism or effect rather than socially interactive agent behavior.

name: HRI
fullName: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
topics: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction
notes: Full papers track. Short contributions and alt.HRI have separate deadlines. Late-breaking reports close December 8, 2026; videos and demos close November 20. These are distinct from the main full-paper track shown here.

publication.note: Nominated papers needing further work may transfer for continued journal review. This is not automatic journal publication.

guide.contribution: Contribute knowledge about human-robot interaction and choose the track that matches it: design, technical work, systems, studies, or theory and methods. Make the human-robot interaction question central.
guide.evidence: Use evaluation appropriate to the track. A technical paper needs robust methods and suitable validation, while a studies paper centers knowledge gained from people. The technical track does not require a user study unless it is appropriate to the contribution.

comparisons.difference: More centered on socially interactive agents, including virtual agents; useful when the contribution concerns agent behavior beyond a robotics setting.
A broader HCI audience when the interaction or design insight extends substantially beyond human-robot interaction.
